newsitem.title: UK: British top the European ranks of chocoholics.
newsitem.headline: British top the European ranks of chocoholics.

text.p: The British are Europe's greatest chocoholics, spending an average of $91.11 per person each year on chocolates, according to a new market report.

Market research group Datamonitor on Monday said its new report, Western European Confectionary, shows the European chocolate market is now worth about $18 billion, up from $16.84 billion in 1992. The total European confectionary market is worth about $30 billion.

The British chocolate market leads Europe at $5.32 billion a year, up from $4.45 billion in 1992. Germany is the second-largest chocolate market at $4.27 billion a year, although the German's consume an average of only $52.01 a year per person, Datamonitor said.

The Irish are the second biggest consumers of chocolate on a per capita basis, spending an average of $90.39 each year, with the Swedish in third place at $88.19 a year. But despite the renowned reputation of Swiss chocolate, the Swiss rank only eighth, spending an average of $64.57 each per year, Datamonitor said.
Trailing the ranking of 16 European countries is Spain, with average chocolate spending a mere $11.64 each, Datamonitor said.
